#699. JoJo Siwa and Chris Hughes Break Up After 1.5 Years of Dating

JoJo Siwa and Chris Hughes, who met while competing on Celebrity Big Brother UK in 2025, split over one year into their relationship, multiple outlets confirmed.

The "Karma" singer has split from former Love Island UK star Chris Hughes after a year and a half together, multiple outlets confirmed.

E! News reached out to reps for the pair for comment but has not yet heard back.

Siwa, 23, and Hughes, 33, first met in 2025 on the set of Celebrity Big Brother UK. While the Dance Moms alum was dating podcaster Kath Ebbs at the time, she formed a close bond with Hughes during the reality competition series.

"I've always told myself I'm a lesbian and I think being here, I’ve realized: ‘Oh, I’m not a lesbian, I’m queer,'" she told housemate Danny Beard at the time. "And I think that’s really cool."

Siwa broke up from Ebbs shortly after the show's finale in May, with her and Hughes going public with their romance the following month.

“It’s not platonic anymore,” Siwa admitted in a June 2025 interview with The Guardian, “and it’s been a beautiful development, a beautiful connection, and I’m absolutely head over heels for him and he’s the same way.”

The "Boomerang" artist also clarified her sexuality, emphasizing that she still considers herself to be a proud member of the LGBTQ+ community.

"I think the most beautiful term now is queer,” Siwa told E! News that same month. "There's loads of beautiful, different sexualities. Sexuality and queerness is a lovely rainbow that has all different places, and it also has places on this rainbow that we don't even know exist yet.”

She continued, "What I realized with Christopher is I never have second guessed my feelings for him. Therefore, I've never second guessed my happiness, I've never second guessed what I'm feeling. And I think that's the most beautiful thing.”

By July, Hughes declared Siwa to be "literally the love of my life."

"She's also my best friend," he noted to E! in a separate interview. "Like, we sit and do nothing together."

At the time, the Chris & Kem musician shared he was ready to take the next steps with Hughes during their first Christmas together, when he gifted her a $2,600 Cartier ring. However, he noted that it wasn't necessarily a marriage proposal because "you always get people who get engaged on Christmas."

As Hughes explained to The Sun, “I like the idea of it not being at a time where it could be expected."

For a look back at more stars who have called it quits this year, keep reading.

The Dancing With the Stars co-host confirmed her break up with the Peloton instructor after a brief romance.

The split came just two days after Williams soft-launched his relationship with Hough on social media, sharing a photo of her holding her dog Sunny to his Instagram Stories, which she’d then reshared to her own account.

The Dancing With the Stars pro confirmed his breakup with the OnlyFans model after nearly one year of dating, telling Us Weekly on Nov. 10, "I'm single."

"We just decided to go our separate ways," he added, "and I’m taking my own time."

The WNBA stars and Dallas Wings teammates confirmed they had broken up "over a year ago" in November 2026.

"We’re still friends, we’re still cool," Bueckers said during an appearance on Fudd's Fudd Around and Find Out podcast. "We broke up over a year ago, so we played an entire season together. We’re the utmost professional. We care about basketball.”

Nearly five months after announcing her pregnancy, the Secret Lives of Mormon Wives star filed for divorce from her husband of seven years on Nov. 3, according to Utah court records obtained by E! News.

In October, multiple outlets confirmed that the eight-time Super Bowl-winning coach and former Bridgewater State University cheerleader ended their relationship in late 2025 after about four years of dating.

The Selling Sunset alum shared an emotional video announcement confirming that she and the Australian musician “are no longer together” three years after tying the knot in 2023.

“We have agreed to treat this public separation with love and respect for each other," Stuase said in an Instagram post Oct. 26. "That’s not hard for me because I am in love with this person.”

The Friday Night Lights alum and the Imagine Dragons member broke up after almost four years together, according to multiple outlets.

The two had confirmed their romance in November 2022 and made their official red carpet debut on May 30, 2026.

Three months after confirming they were separated, the Real Housewives of Salt Lake City star filed for divorce in Utah.

The trailer for the seventh season of RHOSLC revealed just how strained the relationship between the Wild Rose Beauty founder and her husband had become.

The Hills alum confirmed her romance with the "Whiskey and Rain" singer had ended after two years of dating.

The "Mi Gente" singer (real name José Álvaro Osorio Balvín) and the model broke up after nearly 10 years of dating.

"After sharing so many years and important moments together, Jose and I have decided to go our separate ways," Ferrer wrote on her instagram Story Sept. 16. "It has been a decision made out of love, respect, and the desire to do the best for our family."

Noting that co-parenting son Rio "with all our love" is top priority, she added, "We are living this process with ease and deeply appreciate the understanding and respect towards this time so personal to us."

“We have been separated for a while, and it’s proven to be the right move for us and our family unit," the Mean Girls alum and the Newsroom actor told People in a joint statement Sept. 15. "We’ve got each other forever—and it’s GOOD."

On Aug. 19, multiple outlets reported that the Fifty Shades of Grey star and the "Sally, When the Wine Runs Out" singer broke up less than one year after sparking dating rumors.

The Fashion Police alum confirmed her split from the musician amid reports that he had been fired from Slipknot, writing on Instagram Stories Aug. 3, "Strange how the loudest defense of the guilty is rarely innocence… It’s distraction."

"I will not take your s--t anymore! I’m done,” she added. "Leave me alone. Let me heal. I can’t protect you from yourself anymore."

The Empire actress confirmed the former couple had called off their engagement and ended their three-year relationship in a lengthy Instagram statement.

"I loved deeply," Serayah wrote in the Aug. 25 post. "Believed wholeheartedly in the life we were building, and wanted nothing more than to protect our family."

“It has been a sad and difficult situation, but we have been focused on navigating the change privately and positively for a healthy and happy co parenting environment for our son, and ourselves,” the pair—parents to Sky Safir Cornish Colman—shared in a July 20 statement. “Unfortunately being in the public eye this is the easiest way to let people know the truth, before rumours circulate or a false narrative is written.”

The pair, who share 15-year-old daughter Elektra, tied the knot in June 1999 and have since built a hair salon empire, which they co-own.

After the Las Culturistas podcast host and Below Deck star began dating in the summer of 2025 following an Instagram meet-cute, E! News confirmed July 16 that the pair mutually decided to part ways and remain friends.

The Malcolm in the Middle star shared that he and Price were splitting up after six years of marriage.

“After 10 beautiful years together, we’ve grown in ways that made us realize our relationship feels most natural and strong as a deep friendship and as co-parents,” Muniz and Price wrote in a joint Instagram post July 1. “We share an incredible son who remains the center of our world, and we’re both happier, stronger parents because of the love and growth we’ve shared.”

The Grey’s Anatomy alum confirmed in May that she and her husband—who share kids Noah, Taeyln and Anniston—quietly broke up after more than two decades of marriage.

Despite ending their romance the couple's rep emphasized the remain on "great terms" and are committed to coparenting their sons Sid and Lazlo.

"I've made the decision to end my relationship with Klay," the rapper told E! News in an April 25 statement. "Trust, fidelity and respect are non-negotiable for me in a relationship, and when those values are compromised, there's no real path forward."

The statement came shortly after Megan accused the NBA star of cheating, writing on her Instagram Story, "Holding you down through all your HORRIBLE mood swings and treatment towards me during your basketball season now you don't know if you can be 'monogamous'????"

Megan and Sue added, “We've shared a whole life over the last decade, through big moments and in quiet ones, and that is something we'll always carry with us.”

The Real Housewives of New York star's husband filed for divorce on April 2 after nine years of marriage, according to a court docket viewed by E! News.

In the filing, David is listed as the plaintiff, filing for a summons and complaint, or instigation of a lawsuit. Sai—mom to London and Rio with David—is listed as the defendant and has yet to address the filing publicly.

#698. Man City owners should be forced to sell, say clubs

The independent commission is yet to decide on a sanction for Manchester City

Manchester City's owners must be forced to sell up as punishment for it breaking financial rules, senior figures at some Premier League clubs have told BBC Sport.

This week, the chair of the Independent Football Regulator (IFR) David Kogan claimed he has the "stomach" to take action against City, who deny wrongdoing and have appealed.

The IFR has the power to remove directors of a club if they are deemed unsuitable, and even force a sale in the most serious cases.

Now, officials at three top-flight clubs have told the BBC that they believe this is the appropriate punishment for City, who were found guilty of breaching Premier League financial regulations between 2009 and 2018, and failing to co-operate with an investigation.

Premier League clubs to cover legal costs if Man City sponsors sue

Rival clubs want range of punishments for Man City

The independent commission has yet to decide on a sanction that could range from a fine, to a points deduction, the stripping of past titles, or even expulsion from the league.

But speaking on condition of anonymity, one executive claimed they are among a group of clubs who feel that City's punishment will be irrelevant unless the owners are also forced to sell. They added that anything less will make them question why they are funding the regulator through a levy.

In comments that reveal the level of anger felt by other clubs, another source claimed the rule breaches had undermined the league's credibility, and that they would not be able to draw a line under the scandal and move on if the owners were allowed to stay. The club were found guilty of inflating revenues and disguising losses by Â£900m through "sham" commercial arrangements.

Manchester City's owners are Abu Dhabi United Group - a private investment company belonging to United Arab Emirates vice-president and deputy Prime Minister Sheikh Mansour.

The official - who also spoke anonymously - said that clubs had been asked by the Premier League to refrain from publicly revealing their views on sanctions, and let the process run its course, although some are said to have privately made their opinions clear to IFR officials. They acknowledged that some clubs were less opinionated about a punishment.

Other clubs the BBC approached declined to comment, or said they were willing for the independent commission panel and IFR to reach their own conclusions following the publication of the commission's ruling in September.

But the fact that some clubs want the unprecedented sanction of a forced sale will put pressure on Kogan to mete out the harshest penalty possible in what is being seen as a defining test of the watchdog just over a year after it was established.

It also comes amid mounting questions over whether wider UAE trade and investment in UK projects could be impacted by such a move. In September, Prime Minister Andy Burnham was criticised for saying he would be "really concerned" if the scandal led to City's owners selling the club, adding that "they have been such a huge partner in the building of modern Manchester".

When approached, the IFR declined to comment. But Kogan has consistently said that the IFR will not be influenced by any political pressure.

Earlier this week he told a parliamentary committee that the watchdog would not be afraid to investigate City's hierarchy and take action, depending on the outcome of the appeal.

"Forget the name of the club, forget the size of the club, forget the scale of the issue. We cannot simply ignore our statutory duties in relation to a club because it happens to be of a certain size," Kogan said.

"We absolutely will have to take the appropriate action as laid out in the legislation, depending on the circumstances as they come to us, which are the evidence that's been presented and collated by the independent commission of the Premier League and by any judgement that takes place on that evidence through an appeal.

"But in one sense, the evidence has already been judged by those cases having been found guilty, so we will absolutely have the stomach to do so... assuming those circumstances are triggered, if we don't act, what is the purpose of having a football regulator?"

Sheikh Mansour's control of Manchester City has come into question

When asked how any potential legal battles with Manchester City would be paid for, IFR chief executive Richard Monks told MPs that a litigation reserve of Â£2m was to be built up over the next two years via the levy charged to clubs, which would be paid back if litigation was successful.

"Now clearly - and I'm not talking about a specific case - clearly, there could be a very large legal case of any particular club that would require us to spend more than Â£2m in terms of litigation costs and barrister costs in particular", Monks added. "So if that happens, we have agreed with government [that it] will effectively lend us the money in terms of cash flow.

"We'd expect to win that litigation, to claim costs and repay government. If we failed in that massive litigation, then ultimately it would be added to the levy and we'd repay government that way."

Last month it was revealed that the IFR would cost clubs in the top five divisions of English men's football Â£20.3m annually.

Last week, Premier League clubs voted to cover legal expenses for its five board directors if any of City's sponsors sued them. Two UAE-based commercial partners - Etihad and Etisalat - have both said they are considering legal action against the Premier League.

The IFR has the authority to force a sale within section 34 of the Football Governance Act which allows it to investigate whether an owner meets the required suitability standards around honest, integrity and financial soundness. If an owner fails this assessment, the regulator can direct them to take reasonable steps to relinquish ownership within a specified period before issuing an ownership removal order.

City have been approached for comment. The club previously said that the commission's ruling contained "clear material errors, of law, principle and fact and is unsafe", adding that they filed "a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence [that] exists in support of all of its positions".

#697. Inspired by Bernie Sanders: A German agency is using US-Style campaigning to boost the left in 2029

"The Goodforces" wants to see a swing to the left in the 2029 German elections. The agency counts New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani and Bernie Sanders among its inspirations. Could it transform the political landscape?

Red, red, green — those are the party colors of the left-leaning coalition recently formed in the German state of Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania. Now a Berlin-based agency wants to see the same alliance between the center-left Social Democrats, the socialist Left Party, and environmentalist Greens win the 2029 national elections.

The Goodforces wants to help make that a reality with their campaign neunund20 (twenty-nine), taking its cue, in part, from the American left. The agency was set up in response to the rise of the far right across Europe.

Co-founder Patrick Haermeyer told DW that the campaign's aim is "to give people hope and an alternative narrative to: Things are getting worse and worse." He worked as an online organizer for the election team of Bernie Sanders in the US Democratic presidential primaries in 2016 and cites Sanders' "not me, us" campaign as an inspiration.

Neunund20 currently has two strategies: It provides digital space for short-form videos and social media content on political and social topics on Instagram, Tiktok, and Bluesky. At the same time, it tries to connect content creators, activists, NGOs, and political initiatives around shared "progressive" issues.

Users with a particular interest can click to get a link giving them access to archives of relevant social media material that they can then reshare. That feature is modelled on the campaign of New York's left-wing mayor Zohran Mamdani.

And there are other projects. The Goodforces was recently involved in a tactical voting initiative in the September elections in the state of Saxony-Anhalt, intended to keep the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) from winning an absolute majority. Haermeyer says physical campaigns of that kind are necessary to provide essential "interim victories" en route to the next parliamentary elections.

The Greens and the SPD, the two parties recommended by the app created by the organization, made it over the 5% hurdle and into parliament. The help that they received was declared by each party in the form of a €40,000 ($43,900) donation.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

The agency sees itself as a kind of Super PAC, modeled on political organizations in the United States that collect money to carry out campaigns without directly supporting a single party or a special candidate.

For Christoph Bieber, political scientist at the University of Duisburg-Essen, the Goodforces is an interesting new type of player on Germany's political scene because it operates outside the country's political parties.

But many of those parties are eyeing the development with disquiet. The far-left, populist, immigration skeptical Alliance for Social Justice and Economic Reason (BSW) criticized the Goodforces' intervention in Saxony-Anhalt, telling the newspaper FAZ that it was an "infantilizing, and perhaps even antidemocratic action." The neoliberal Free Democrats (FDP) called the tool "wrong and intentionally misleading." The FDP failed to clear the threshold, while the BSW only just squeaked in. The AfD gained 43% of the vote and its candidate may soon become Germany's first far-right state premier since the Nazi era.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Haermeyer set up the agency in 2024 along with Peter Jelinek, and both men previously worked for Green Party European Parliament member Michael Bloss. Ahead of that year's European elections, the EU's Green Deal began to come under increasing attack.

That year also ended with the collapse of Germany's first federal coalition between the SPD, Greens, and FDP, after much infighting and attacks from right-wing quarters.

"We noticed that more and more successes and freedoms that we had fought for were being reversed: Things like freedom of movement, border checks, and other things that were coming more and more under fire," Haermeyer told DW. "And we noticed that it was primarily democratic and progressive forces that were being drawn into defensive battles."

The AfD, founded in 2013, already in the age of social media, has successfully targeted younger voters with in its online campaigns. But the older parties, in particular, have struggled. The Goodforces saw a need for support in the online environment and is now seeking to plug this gap.

The social media accounts of the campaign neunund20 contain posts on domestic German topics, such as the current negotiations to form a red-red-green coalition government in Berlin, and the country's new military service law. They also highlight "wins" in Spain in the protests for affordable housing and for US Democrats in the midterms.

Haermeyer stresses that the issues the agency highlights are determined together with a wide range of grassroots organizations and activists. "The campaign is not agreed in conjunction with the SPD, the Left Party, and the Greens," he said.

Agency funding comes from commissions and small donations. Haermeyer says that contributions generally range from $20 to $50.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Bieber sees the emergence of non-party campaigning, long an accepted practice in the US, as a bid to compensate for the shortcomings of traditional parties.

"It is an omission of the parties," he said. "For years they have been saying we have to modernize, we have to become more open and get away from rigid membership structures. There are legal regulations governing the organization of political parties in Germany, but perhaps it could be more flexible and open."

The center-left and center-right big-tent parties have been in decline for decades. Membership of the SPD dropped from 943,000 in 1990 to some 348,000 at the end of 2025. Chancellor Friedrich Merz's Christian Democratic Union (CDU) has seen a fall from 750,000 to under 357,000.

Party membership is particularly low in former communist eastern Germany. Centrist parties have also struggled to attract younger voters. A report by the Deutsche Kinder und Jugendstiftung (German Children and Youth Foundation) showed that only 20% of young people felt their concerns were taken seriously in the 2025 German elections and that trust in parties was low.

In the United States, campaign financing comes predominantly from donations, and lobby groups can buy influence by contributing unlimited amounts to super PACs. In Germany, party funding comes, in part, from taxpayers and membership fees, and donations are capped. However, Bieber warns that whereas there are strict rules regarding the disclosure of donors to US Super PACs, these do not exist in Germany.

The political scientist does not believe that US-style campaigning is going to take hold in Germany, but he does see potential dangers: "This could be a door opener to make others consider whether they want to go in this direction in the field of campaigning. And he added: "If it becomes rife, it could lead to a further devaluation of parties and their structures."

#696. Emery praises Garnacho attitude after Villa selection snub

Garnacho has not played for Aston Villa since making a three-minute cameo in a 1-1 draw against Fulham on 31 October.

Aston Villa boss Unai Emery has praised Alejandro Garnacho's "fantastic attitude" -but suggested other players rank ahead of him after the Argentine was left out of Tuesday's Champions League defeat at Galatasaray.

The 22-year-old winger joined Aston Villa on loan from Chelsea in the summer, but he has played just 34 minutes in the Premier League this season.

Garnacho was left at home for the 2-0 loss by Galatasaray, with Emery bringing 11 substitutes - including two goalkeepers - rather than the maximum 12.

"When he is not involved in the squad it is because I have to choose with other players as well," said the Villa boss on Friday.

"He has my respect first as a person and second as a player, but he is not involved for this reason.

"But football can change. We are playing matches so I will need players."

Not even making a 12-man bench - what next for Garnacho?

Garnacho has played in just four of Villa's 11 Premier League matches this season and has yet to start across all competitions, coming off the bench for all seven of his appearances.

His last appearance - just a three-minute cameo - came in the 1-1 draw against Fulham on 31 October.

"Alejandro Garnacho is training very well. His attitude is fantastic, very good attitude," Emery added.

"He was struggling at the beginning of the season because he was not fit. Now he is fit and he's training at a good level."

Sources have acknowledged Garnacho was not at the level required and were surprised how off the pace he was when he signed in July.

He initially trained on his own, while his problems were not helped by a head injury suffered in Thailand in pre-season.

"Of course now he, and other players as well, are performing well, they are working well, they understood how we are building the squad," Emery said.

"It's not how it was two months ago when he wasn't fit enough to be playing with the consistency we needed.

"So keep going, keep moving forward as a club, as a team, he himself as a player and we will see it."

Garnacho's move to Villa will become permanent for Â£43m at the end of the season should certain criteria be met, but there are concerns his time at the club could become similar to that of Harvey Elliot, who played just nine times last season after arriving on loan from Liverpool.

Fifa rules allow players to play for two clubs in a season - or three if they move to a team whose season overlaps like the Major League Soccer - meaning Garnacho could feature for another team, unlike Elliott as he had already played for Liverpool and Villa.

However, Emery said he was not thinking about the upcoming January transfer window as he added: "It is November, of course there is a transfer window in January, but we are not thinking about the transfer window in January. Me especially."

Does this damage Villa after Elliott lost a year of his career last season?

There was already talk in the game of how players could be fearful it could happen to them - and that caution may increase with Garnacho's situation.

Having happened twice in two seasons it would also leave clubs with second thoughts too given the players are their assets.

Garnacho has managed just 95 minutes across all competitions, having joined Villa to revive a faltering career after an inconsistent first season at Chelsea.

Head of football operations Damian Vidagany was unrepentant when asked about the winger at a fans' forum on Thursday, with Emery's trusted lieutenant fiercely backing the manager's judgement call.

Villa, though, arguably need a player like Garnacho - who can produce moments of magic like his stunning goal for Manchester United against Everton in 2023 - having failed to score in four of their last six winless games.

Emery wanted a pacy winger in the summer and the Argentine had been on their wanted list all year.

They need some need some creativity, so with Emery, at least publicly, refusing to rule out a January departure there could still be a slim chance of redemption.

#694. 'I am not a magician' - what can Maresca's Man City learn from watertight Arsenal?

Manchester City have managed only five clean sheets this season

Manchester City's leaky defence faces one of its most difficult tasks of the season with a trip to watertight Arsenal, aiming to put right their patchy recent form.

Enzo Maresca's side began the season with eight straight victories but have won only one of their past seven in all competitions inside 90 minutes and head to Emirates Stadium trailing the champions by six points even at this early juncture.

A Premier League defeat on Sunday could well have long-term consequences for City's title aspirations, with Mikel Arteta's men clearly standing above any other top-flight side as the ones to topple.

Though the Gunners dropped points last weekend with a draw at Newcastle, they continue to set the standards with a miserly defence that has conceded only seven goals in the club's opening 11 league games.

Asked why he felt City have dropped off in recent weeks, Maresca - who replaced Pep Guardiola as manager in the summer - said: "For me it's because we've had four months together. Transition requires time.

"It's probably because we won seven games in a row, with Champions League eight in a row. Everyone was thinking at City there's no transition but I've said many times I am not a magician. There is transition, it's normal.

"There are eight or nine new players, the manager is new so you need time and you can see different clubs when they had transition how complicated it is. For me, it's completely normal, I'm completely relaxed, no panic at all."

'Pass, pass, slow, slow' - Man City's slick machine grinding to a halt

Why Man City can't wear their new kit in Premier League

"We are conceding too many goals and we need to avoid that," was an obvious statement made by Maresca following last Saturday's 1-1 draw against Fulham.

City followed that up with another home stalemate against Napoli in the Champions League on Tuesday and have now conceded in 10 successive games in all competitions for the first time in seven years.

"[It was] far, far too easy to play through [City]," said former England captain Alan Shearer of Rodrigo Muniz's goal for Fulham on Match of the Day.

"Fulham's throw-in was level with their own 18-yard box. For them to get through is not acceptable at any level, let alone when you are playing for Manchester City and Muniz ran past the entire midfield [to score]."

City have managed only five clean sheets all campaign, which is in stark contrast to Arsenal, who have kept double the amount so far, while Newcastle's opening goal ended a run off 445 minutes without the ball hitting their net.

Maresca's men also have an issue by conceding the opener, having done so seven times in the past 10 games, and of the 14 goals they have shipped, six have come inside the first 20 minutes.

An early Arsenal goal may well be an important factor in deciding Sunday's contest.

Asked how his side can improve defensively, Maresca said: "Video [analysis], meetings, [on] pitch coaching, It is a mix of that.

"Some of the goals we concede we can avoid, so hopefully we can do that."

Man City fan questions what's behind Marc Guehi's recent struggles

The injury to key defender William Saliba has almost gone unnoticed for Arsenal as Ezri Konsa has stepped in to fill the void at centre-back seamlessly since joining from Aston Villa in the summer.

The England international has established a formidable partnership with Gabriel and the two have quickly formed an impressive understanding this season.

Maresca, meanwhile, admitted he was still "trying to find different" solutions to his team, which has been highlighted by the chopping and changing of his backline.

In 16 Premier League and Champions League games this season, the Italian has used eight different combinations in defence, which has given players little chance of fostering any sort of on-pitch relationships with each other.

City have also made seven errors leading to goals, compared to Arsenal's one.

"You are concerned in some way because that is a lot of errors leading to goals," said former City defender Nedum Onuoha. "With some of the best players you ask, 'what are they really good at?' For some it is the fact they don't make mistakes.

"They are ruthless and relentless in the way they play but at this moment in time City are being punished for those errors.

"A manager can have the tactics and do the team talks, but if people are going to continue to make those mistakes, they will suffer."

The chant of "1-0 to the Arsenal" has been synonymous with the Gunners over the years and it could not be more apt under Arteta.

Since the start of last season, his side have won 16 matches in all competitions by that particular scoreline, compared to six by City.

After beating Sunderland in a chaotic match in September, Maresca said he would "prefer to win 1-0 than 5-3", suggesting his side needed more control and he re-iterated that message after the Fulham draw.

"Sometimes you need to win games 1-0 for a small difference and to keep a clean sheet but in this moment we are not able to do that," he admitted.

City, though, have scored five more league goals than Arsenal in this campaign and Sunday's hosts have injury concerns over goalkeeper David Raya.

The Spaniard is a doubt with the shoulder problem he picked up at Newcastle, and compatriot Kepa Arrizabalaga may deputise again as he did in the 1-1 draw against Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League on Tuesday.

City have fond memories of coming up against Arsenal's stand-in keeper, after Kepa's howler for the opening goal contributed to their 2-0 Carabao Cup final triumph back in March.

A repeat result on Sunday will provide a much-needed morale boost for Maresca and his team.

#693. Sutton's predictions v Kings of Leon drummer Nathan Followill

Arsenal co-chairman Josh Kroenke should probably turn his phone off if the Gunners fall behind against Manchester City on Sunday.

Chris Sutton's predictions guest this week, Kings of Leon drummer and City fan Nathan Followill, is good friends with Kroenke - and says he will be in touch if the game is going City's way.

"I'm super excited for this weekend and I've got my smack talk ready for Josh already," Followill told BBC Sport.

"I've heard about the City fans with their inflatable bananas and I need to get myself one. My wife is going to be like 'er, an inflatable banana just arrived in the mail - do you know anything about that?'

"We are going to win 4-2 so I will be texting Josh throughout the game... and, after Erling Haaland's second goal, I will send him a picture of me kissing the banana!"

AI has also made its predictions, and you can pick your own below.

The most popular scoreline selected for each game is used in the scoreboards and tables at the bottom of this page.

A correct result (picking a win, draw or defeat) is worth 10 points. The exact score earns 40 points.

Want to make more predictions? You can play BBC Sport's new Match of the Day predictor game every week, featuring six fixtures from domestic and European competition.

Followill got a behind the scenes tour of Etihad Stadium and City's training complex when Kings of Leon played next door at Co-op Live arena in 2024. "It's a beautiful stadium, and an amazing set-up," he said. "Their practice pitches are better than most college pitches in the US."

Followill has supported City for more than 20 years, external and his children have followed in his footsteps by becoming Blues, despite the best efforts of his next-door neighbour in Nashville, as well as Kroenke.

"When my kids were born, they both received a full Arsenal kit - head to toe - in the mail from Josh," he explained.

"Both times, they were returned to sender - instantly.

"My son and daughter are both City fans now, but my neighbour, Jeremy Connor, is Tottenham, and I mean flying the flag full on.

"When they lose, you can hear him screaming - and when they win, you can hear him screaming too.

"His son is trying to convert my son to Spurs and I am like 'that is never going to happen in this house!'"

Chris Sutton and Nathan Followill were speaking to BBC Sport's Chris Bevan.

The AI predictions were generated using Microsoft Copilot Chat - we simply asked the tool to 'predict this weekend's Premier League scores'.

Followill says it was eye-opening to watch City's boys and girls' teams play when he visited their training campus. "I had no idea how much they put into developing kids from the youngest ages all the way up," he said. "That was probably the most impressive thing for me - to see how many young kids were out there, with the ultimate dream of pulling on that blue shirt one day."

Chelsea have scored and conceded 20 goals so far this season, which kind of sums up where they are at.

Xabi Alonso's side have also lost as many league games - five - as Manchester United, and United are in crisis.

Alonso is not under pressure, or anything like that, but if they lose this game too, you can imagine the mood of the club - and it won't be good.

Apparently their fans were singing 'you don't know what you're doing' at him after their defeat by Leeds - which is what they sang at me when I was there.

Alonso needs to decide on a shape and a way of playing, and stick with it.

Anything could happen here, because Nottingham Forest's form is hardly convincing either.

They tore Manchester City apart in their previous home game, before the international break, but can they really dig out another result like that here?

I think they will go about it in a similar way, and be aggressive and have a real go at Chelsea... and I don't see Chelsea's defence keeping them out.

Nathan's prediction: No-one thought Forest would beat us, and while Chelsea need a big result, I can see Forest getting a point here. 1-1

We talked about Leeds on the Monday Night Club and how they have upgraded their team with the players Daniel Farke bought over the summer.

Farke strengthened in the areas he needed to improve, but is still trusting some of the players who did well for him last season - the likes of Jayden Bogle and James Justin, who have been outstanding.

They are a really well-balanced team and they have good depth to their squad too. The only criticism would be that they are not usually free-scoring - they hit four against Chelsea but before then they had only managed 10 goals in their first 10 league games.

Leeds do not give much away at the back either, though, and I think that will be key in this game.

When I watch Coventry they are dynamic with their counter-attacks and I always fancy them to nick a goal like that.

Not this time, however. Leeds might take a while to break them down, but I think they will come out on top.

Nathan's prediction: Coventry play in sky blue too? Part of the reason I became a Manchester City fan was the kit, and I have always gravitated towards teams in light blue, so I am going to go with Coventry here. 0-1

I am at this game for 5 Live and I am not expecting much to change for Manchester United.

No-one thought it was going to be easy for Mauricio Pochettino to go in at United and turn things around. He has taken over a complete rabble.

United's draw in Lisbon on Wednesday was chaotic, but you also have to consider how Sporting have not got going in the Portuguese league or the Champions League this season.

That was not a great Sporting side. They are pretty average and Brentford will be a much bigger test.

The Bees are supremely well-organised and will be full of confidence, too, after putting four goals past Everton on Monday. They were against 10 men for the entire second half, but were 2-0 up by then anyway.

Pochettino needs something to cling to, but for him picking that backline must be like pinning the tail on the donkey. Whoever he picks, they are not very good.

I really want to be more positive about United, because I heard from quite a few of their fans last weekend, but this prediction is about as positive as I can be about them at the moment.

Nathan's prediction: It is tough for me to talk about United because in America we have a saying 'don't kick a man when he's down' and it's pretty rough for them right now... but I'm not going to lie, it is nice to see United this low in the table.

I don't think it is the manager that is the problem for United right now, so I don't think Pochettino coming in is going to be an instant fix. They've got some growing pains to get through, and I won't be disappointed to watch that.

When I watch the Premier League at home, Brentford always cracks me up because I am huge fan of The Office and I just imagine a bunch of David Brents out there, just running around the pitch, which is a very funny thing for me.

I know I just said don't kick a man when he's down, but I don't think United would be nice to us if we were down there... so, I think the David Brents are going to win. 1-2

I actually think Villa will win this game 2-1 but I want to make it clear the scoreline I have gone for is from my commentary colleague, Alistair Bruce-Ball, who is an Ipswich fan - a fake one, but still a fan.

I asked him about this game when we were in Belgium for Liverpool's Champions League game on Wednesday. He will be at Portman Road on Saturday for 5 Live and he is backing the Tractor Boys to get something, so I am doing the same out of respect for him.

Ipswich really need a result too. They have gone five league games without a win and, with Hull and Coventry both winning last week, they are the lowest placed of the promoted sides.

That is never a good thing, and it feels like Gary O'Neil's side are in a precarious position at the moment, where they are getting sucked towards the bottom three.

I've been surprised to see Villa hit a bit of a sticky patch too, with three successive league draws and no wins in six in all competitions, so it will be interesting to see if they are any better here.

Nathan's prediction: Villa have had some surprising results recently but I do think they will win this. 1-3

I was in Bruges to watch Liverpool in midweek and it was interesting to see two of their players who came in for some heavy flak last season, Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz, both shine.

Isak is looking like the player who Liverpool thought they signed in 2025. He is finding his rhythm, and Wirtz also seems to be in a really good place confidence-wise. When I watch them now, it feels like something is going to happen.

There are other positives for Reds boss Andoni Iraola too. I know there will be a debate about Bradley Barcola's end-product but I love watching him in full flow when he is running past defenders - there is no better sight in football than moments like that.

Rio Ngumoha is exciting as well, and he has such a good football brain which makes him even more dangerous.

Everything points to a Liverpool win, but I am hesitant to just go with that because Everton are coming off the back of a drubbing by Brentford. You can imagine David Moyes giving his side a miserable old week and getting stuck into his players.

I didn't think James Tarkowski should have been sent off in that game, but he will be suspended here. It is his absence that swings it for me because he is a real leader for Everton.

Nathan's prediction: Everton are usually the underdogs in this game but both teams are pretty level at the moment. One of our record producers is a huge Liverpool fan so he won't be happy with me... but I am going to say Everton will take it. 2-1

I was at Newcastle's draw with Arsenal last week and, in fairness to Magpies boss Matthias Jaissle, he changed things around at half-time and got his reward.

Jaissle needed that half of football, because I don't think the Newcastle fans have been too convinced by his approach, but this is another very tough game for him.

Brighton probably still can't believe they lost to Hull last week - but lightning is not going to strike twice.

Nathan's prediction: I have to give a shout out to my statistician Lucy here, because there were a couple of teams I didn't know a lot about and she gave me some good insight. So, Brighton have scored a lot of goals this season and I think they will get more here. 3-1

Thomas Frank has got a huge task at Crystal Palace. They are conceding so many goals.

Losing Maxence Lacroix and Marc Guehi from their defence was like Robbie Williams and Jason Orange leaving Take That, because they were never going to be the same without them.

I still think Frank has got some decent attacking players, however.

The Hull keeper, Konstantinos Tzolakis, looks like a great signing. I don't know how he made some of his saves against Brighton and he probably doesn't know himself either.

Brighton should have buried them and I think Palace will get plenty of chances too.

Fair play to Hull for their spirit and the way they scrap for each other, but I still think they are going to go down.

Hull fans are probably wondering if I am ever going to predict they will win a game... the answer is no, at least not this week anyway.

Nathan's prediction: Palace have given up 27 goals in 11 games which is a lot. Hull have surprised a few people this season and I am backing them here. 0-2

Bournemouth are on a long winning run in the league but I've been impressed by Fulham whenever I've watched them.

Alvaro Arbeloa's side have not been great at home, with only one win at Craven Cottage so far, so I am going with them to get another draw - which would be their fourth in a row.

Nathan's prediction: Both these teams have picked up a lot, so this is a tough one to call. 2-2

Tottenham boss Roberto de Zerbi must think a lot of 18-year-old midfielder Luca Williams-Barnett after picking him for their win over Ipswich.

I love to see managers trust young players like that, especially because Spurs have had such a tricky season so far.

It will be interesting to see whether De Zerbi picks him again here, but I feel like the outcome of this game is more dependent on which Sunderland we see.

They picked up a good point at Villa last time out, but they never seem to be quite the same after they have played in Europe, like they are doing this week.

The Black Cats will be without injured duo Brian Brobbey and Granit Xhaka for this game too, so I don't think they will have enough to win it.

Nathan's prediction: Dave Stewart from Eurythmics lives in Nashville too and is a good buddy of mine - and he is Sunderland until death! He is such a die-hard fan that every time we have dinner, we will sit there and talk about 'Haway the Lads' and just shoot the breeze about Sunderland.

So I am going to back them in this one, because of Dave and also because of my neighbour Jeremy, who I mentioned earlier.

Jeremy was especially cocky when they had Harry Kane and he would just talk so much smack - I always knew if they were doing good because I'd get a text from him. So, because Jeremy is such a cocky little Spurs fan, I am saying Sunderland will win. 2-1

I always enjoy this game because of Gabriel's battle with Erling Haaland, but it is in midfield where I think it will be decided.

Manchester City have spent a lot of money on players in that part of the pitch but Enzo Maresca has not found the right combination yet.

Somehow Maresca has got to find a way of nullifying Declan Rice, but that will be very difficult because Rice is just an absolute machine.

You can never rule City out because of Haaland's ability to score goals but the only result I see here is an Arsenal win, and I am going for a classic Gunners scoreline.

Nathan's prediction: This is the big one! It's huge. I feel really good about it, too. Arsenal are riding so high at the moment, I feel like we might catch them snoozing.

I predict Haaland will get two goals, Phil Foden will get one too and we will end up with four. 2-4

After drawing a blank since week two, Chris finally picked up another win in week 11 - and it was his spot-on prediction for Liverpool to thump Manchester United 4-0 that sealed the deal.

That meant he got three correct results, including two exact scores - at Anfield, and Tottenham's 2-0 win over Ipswich - giving him a total of 90 points.

In a tricky week for predictions, where Liverpool were the only team to start the weekend in the Premier League's top six who won, it was those exact scores that made all the difference.

Chris' guest, undisputed world champion boxer Lauren Price, the BBC readers and AI also all got three correct results.

But the BBC readers were the only ones to also get an exact score - in the Spurs game - giving them 60 points.

Lauren and AI both ended up on 30 points - AI did call Newcastle's draw with Arsenal correctly, but it was wrong about Bournemouth's win over Nottingham Forest, which everyone else got right.

Not many of you got that Liverpool-United scoreline correct, either.

From around 27,000 predictions, the most popular scoreline picked was a 2-1 home win and only 570 of you went for 4-0.

"When has AI ever gone for a 4-0?" said Sutton. "That's what the crowd wants. The crowd don't want AI - who wants mathematics?

"The crowd want gut-feeling and instinct. I think I should get 1,000 points for that prediction, because I was brave enough to go for it."

For the first time this season, there were SIX games where no-one made a correct prediction - who thought it was easy?

The biggest shock of the week was Leeds' 4-1 victory at Stamford Bridge. Again from around 27,000 predictions, more than 3,600 (14%) of you did back Daniel Farke's side to win... but just 11 of you saw that scoreline coming.

#692. How JoJo Siwa and Chris Hughes’ Romance Unraveled After 1.5 Years

After JoJo Siwa and Chris Hughes fell in love on Celebrity Big Brother, their relationship was unable to stand the test of time, ending a year and a half later.

JoJo Siwa has long danced to the beat of her own drum, and she’s back to doing it alone.

While Siwa came out as a lesbian in 2023 after previously describing herself as pansexual, the Dance Moms alum proved sexuality can be an ever-evolving spectrum when she revealed she and British reality star Chris Hughes had fallen in love.

What began as a close bond while filming Celebrity Big Brother in the UK soon turned into something more after the season wrapped in the spring of 2025, as the pair confirmed their romance that May.

In the time since, Siwa reflected on how meeting Hughes changed what she thought she’d understood about her sexuality, having “always been grossed out by dudes.”

“Chris is a very conventionally hot dude,” she explained on the Wildmen podcast in September. “[But] I thought [he] was just another friend. Once I realized that I wasn't grossed out by the thought of him being a boy, I was like, ‘Whoa.’ It was weird because I'd never thought that before.”

In fact, as she’d never felt a spark for her “conventionally hot” male friends, Siwa was taken aback when her feelings for Hughes began to trend towards the romantic in the Big Brother house, admitting, “I just never thought it was possible.”

And though she also noted Hughes was “very much so the special dude” that could break her previous assumptions about her sexuality, Siwa has also been candid about how previously labeling herself as lesbian never quite felt right.

"I did that because of the pressure," Siwa—who dated Kylie Prew, Avery Cyrus and Kath Ebbs prior to Hughes—told the Daily Mail in 2025. “You just get put in this world where you feel like, because you now have said, 'Oh, I'm a lesbian,' you have to be a lesbian."

But everything changed after meeting Hughes, with the pair both raving about their connection.

“I feel so relaxed and at ease with where I'm at,” Siwa told E! News in July 2025. “I feel so happy and peaceful that the love that I feel is so real. You can't really help who you fall in love with.”

And the feeling was more than mutual, with Hughes telling E! that same month, “She's literally the love of my life, but she's also my best friend. Like, we sit and do nothing together."

And with hopes expressed for future babies and rings given at Christmastime in the months after, it seemed like Siwa and Hughes were in it for the long haul.

That is until Nov. 2026, when their breakup was confirmed by multiple outlets.

Though neither Hughes nor Siwa shared additional insight into their split in the immediate wake of the news, the breakup came as a shock to fans.

After all, just days earlier Siwa confirmed “having a baby” was at the top of her personal agenda during an appearance on the Petticoats Revolution podcast.

“Obviously that's not a career thing,” she continued, “but like a life thing.”

Now, however, it would appear Siwa will need to look elsewhere to start that next chapter.

For a complete look back at Siwa and Hughes’ road to romance, and their abrupt end, read on.

The couple's whirlwind romance unfolded for the whole world to see during their appearance on Celebrity Big Brother.

A year later, Siwa—who split from ex Kath Ebbs following her time on the U.K. the series—released the song "Serendipity" in honor of the now-couple's chance encounter.

"The only word to explain what happened on this day a year ago… Serendipity," Siwa wrote in an Instagram post. "Today, I’m reminded of the moment that quietly changed everything."

Less than a month after they put their bond on display in the Big Brother house and emphasizing they were just friends, Hughes and Siwa confirmed they were dating in late May 2025.

At the time, Siwa cheekily nodded at the romance during a cover of "Bette Davis Eyes" at one of her shows, in which she instead sang "Chris Hughes' eyes."

The Love Island alum joined Siwa at several stops of her Infinity Heart Tour, which spanned across Europe, the U.K. and the United States. In a sweet glimpse at their backstage moments, Siwa added of the tour in an Instagram post, "The show represents who I want to be as a person and the artist that I wanna be in this lifetime, and it’s translated so well to the crowd."

Siwa and Hughes stepped out for their first red carpet as a couple at the Dancers Against Cancer's 2025 Gala of the Stars in Beverly Hills, California.

Siwa shared a glimpse into the couple's favorite bonding activity: golfing in a sweet Instagram photo dump of her summertime adventures.

In September 2026, Hughes gave his followers a slice of life moment by filming Siwa arriving to his place in England—and naturally they shared a sweet embrace to boot.

October 2026: Coming Back Like a Boomerang

Siwa and Hughes turned the Gala of the Stars into a date night two years in a row by attending again in 2026.

Siwa proved her love for Hughes knows no bounds by teasing her next big step in life was to become a mom.

"That’s my next thing," Siwa teased during a Nov. 2026 appearance on the Petticoat Revolution podcast. "Career is doing her thing. She’s always there. She's been there for 15 years. She'll keep going, she'll keep being there.”

Just days after Siwa expressed her hopes for a baby, her breakup with Hughes was confirmed by multiple outlets, marking an end to their romance 1.5 years after it began.

#691. Head coach Slegers leaves Arsenal 18 months after Champions League win

Renee Slegers initially joined Arsenal in 2023 as an assistant coach under Jonas Eidevall

Arsenal have parted company with head coach Renee Slegers by mutual consent after a disappointing start to the season.

Slegers, 37, was initially appointed on an interim basis in October 2024 before being handed the role permanently three months later.

The Dutchwoman led Arsenal to their second Women's Champions League title in May 2025 and the inaugural Fifa Women's Champions Cup in February 2026.

But she leaves with the team sixth in the Women's Super League after 11 matches - 12 points behind leaders Chelsea.

Assistant coach Aaron D'Antino has also left the club, with assistant Melissa Clarke-Reed placed in interim charge as they begin the search for a permanent replacement.

D'Antino had been part of Arsenal's coaching staff since August 2018.

Arsenal director of women's football Clare Wheatley said the decision had been "extremely difficult".

"In leading us to glory in the Champions League and the inaugural Fifa Champions Cup, Renee has made a significant and lasting contribution to the history of Arsenal Football Club, with close support from Aaron," she said.

"After careful reflection, it is clear that results have been below the expected level, and change is necessary."

Chief executive Richard Garlick paid tribute to both departing coaches, describing Slegers as "a wonderful person" who had played "an integral role in some of the most historic achievements in the club's history".

"Our ambition is to compete for and win major trophies consistently, and our recent results have led us to conclude that a change is necessary to give us the best opportunity to achieve those goals," he added.

Why Arsenal are behind in race for Champions League spots

Slegers' departure comes after weeks of pressure as Arsenal's WSL form continued to deteriorate.

While the Dutch coach delivered the Women's Champions League and Women's Champions Cup, results in the league have fallen below expectations this season.

Arsenal have endured a four-match winless run in the league and their struggles have been particularly stark at their own Emirates Stadium, where they have gone six matches without a victory.

For a side expected to challenge for major trophies every season, those dropped points are damaging as they have fallen well adrift of Chelsea and even eight points behind London City Lionesses, who are in the third Women's Champions League qualification spot.

A lack of goals has been central to Arsenal's struggles. They have scored just 11 times in 11 WSL matches this season - less than half the tally of Chelsea (29), second-placed Manchester City (28) and London City Lionesses (31).

Before Slegers' exit was confirmed on Friday, former Arsenal and England forward Lianne Sanderson had called for the manager to depart.

"I've been a big advocate for Renee to stay in the job, but after the Lyon game [a 2-0 home defeat in the Champions League], I felt this feeling in my stomach that it's time [to part ways]," Sanderson told FourFourTwo, external.

"That was probably the most defeated I have felt. The players weren't fighting, they had just shown nothing, there was no identity.

"The definition of insanity is doing the same thing over and over again and expecting different results."

After Sunday's draw with West Ham, Slegers acknowledged performances and results had fallen short of expectations and made it clear she accepted responsibility.

"I love the club," she said. "We're going through a very, very difficult time, and I take my responsibilities, because the results haven't been good enough.

"In the second half we are chasing again, but we're not creating good enough chances to the final third, from all phases, and the way we get there, it's not the Arsenal standard and we need to do that better.

"But I take my responsibilities in my role."

#689. Tom Brady Weighs In On Aaron Rodgers' Release From the Steelers

Tom Brady shared his thoughts on Aaron Rodgers being released from the Pittsburgh Steelers after Rodgers publicly criticized his coach Mike McCarthy.

Tom Brady is tackling his thoughts on Aaron Rodgers.

The retired NFL star shared his reaction to the quarterback’s release from the Pittsburgh Steelers, particularly after Rodgers made comments about Steelers coach Mike McCarthy sleeping during meetings.

“The sanctity of an NFL locker room is a very sacred place,” Brady told Fox Sports co-host Kevin Burkhardt during the Nov. 26 game between the Dallas Cowboys and Philadelphia Eagles. “And we shouldn't ever lose track of that as players.

“It’s a privilege to be in that locker room,” the 49-year-old continued. “You’re fighting with your teammates. You’re fighting with your coaches. You’re always acting as a team, together. [It] shouldn’t always be the place for private things to become public. That’s what I’ll say.”

The co-hosts also lamented the end of Rodgers’ previously illustrious career, with Burkhardt adding, “For the things that were said about Mike McCarthy and things from Aaron—who is the surefire Hall of Famer—if that's the last pass he throws, that's a really sad way to end.”

Brady agreed, noting that while Rodgers was a “tremendous” athlete, his behavior off the field “has nothing to do with his play style” on the field.

“I was fortunate to be around a lot of great teammates over the years, and what made a great teammate, to me, was you cared about your teammates and your coaches, and you cared about what the team was trying to accomplish,” the Super Bowl champ explained. “That supersedes any individual aspect of your game that you want to promote.”

“Again, I was very fortunate. I was in a great locker room. I played for my teammates. I played for my coaches,” he said. “There’s—nobody wins when the family feuds.”

For Brady, his relationships with his coaches and teammates mattered more than “winning a Super Bowl.” He noted that those bonds “transcend anything you do on the field.”

“It’s just unfortunate,” he shared. “I hate it and I hate to be even talking about it. But I just think it's a privilege to be in the NFL. You want to inspire the next generation of athletes and you always want to do it the right way.”

Brady’s comments came just one day after Rodgers was abruptly cut from the Steelers on Nov. 25, who he’d signed with in June 2025. Just before the news, Rodgers spoke candidly about his difficult relationship with McCarthy, including claiming that the 63-year-old would often fall asleep during important team meetings.

"We were in a quarterback meeting. Mike came in late, sat down and within 10 minutes began snoring," the 42-year-old recounted on the Nov. 25 episode of The Pat McAfee Show. "Woke himself up, was rattling his papers. We all looked around. Five minutes later, you hear the snoring again, and less than five minutes after that, he walks out of the room like nothing happened."

He also said that the NFL coach was "not coming to everything you should be coming to as a play caller,” adding that McCarthy even missed meetings ahead of game day.

For a look at what else Rodgers has shared about the difficult relationships in his life, keep reading.

After growing up "in a really conservative, small-town environment" in Chico, Calif., Aaron Rodgers said in the Netflix docuseries Aaron Rodgers: Enigma, transferring from Butte College to University of California, Berkeley, was admittedly an eye-opening experience for him. "So that was fun, to have my ideologies tested."

But, as he recalled, he was already traveling a path that was taking him further and further away from how he was raised by dad Ed Rodgers and mom Darla Rodgers.

The "white, dogmatic church" he grew up in "didn’t really serve me," Aaron said. "It was very rigid in structure. I'm not a rigid person. Shame, guilt, judgment—it was like, 'We have the truth, our way or the highway, our way is heaven, your way is hell.' Even talking to my parents, it was very black and white. Somebody has to be wrong, somebody has to be right. I just slowly uncoupled from that in high school."

So being in a city like Berkeley "that challenged my beliefs" (and where he was sleeping in on Sunday after games instead of going to church), he continued, "definitely helped me to begin to question more things."

Desperately Seeking Spiritual Enlightenment

After capping off the Green Bay Packers' 2011-12 NFL season with a Super Bowl victory—which, until then, Aaron thought was the holy grail he was seeking—he started to wonder what else was out there.

"I really just desperately wanted to be more than  a football player," he said in the series, "and so I started my spiritual journey."

Aaron got into the teachings of progressive spiritual leader Rob Bell, author of What Is the Bible? (which the athlete is seen reading in the series), and started reading more philosophy and self-help books.

Appreciating what he found to be Rob's inclusive, nonjudgmental approach to faith, "He was a big help for me to totally unravel the religion of my youth," Aaron said in Enigma.

Through his readings, "I found a courage to speak my feelings better," he continued. "So I started to stand up to institutions of my youth, and that was everything from organized religion, my parents, dogma, ideology. That definitely changed the dynamics of my family, because I was just questioning all of it."

Winning a Super Bowl vaulted Aaron to another tier of fame, the athlete recalling how during the summer of 2011 he was "paparazzi'd" for the first time during a trip to Hawaii.

"I was like, 'F--k, life's different now," he said. And after he was on TV more, he added, "my whole ability to move around with relative anonymity changed."

He added, "I didn't do myself any favors with some of the girls I dated after that, that were in the public eye. I definitely hated it at first. Like really despised it. I enjoyed my private life. I enjoyed being able to go places. But from Super Bowl MVP, [league] MVP, State Farm commercials, that got a little more difficult."

While the doc flashed to pictures of him with three famous exes, that was the entirety of what Aaron said about his high-profile relationships with Olivia Munn, Danica Patrick and Shailene Woodley (who, incidentally, he was engaged to and didn't just date).

Olivia, who dated Aaron from 2014 until 2017, denied rumors that she played a role in her ex's estrangement from his family, saying on Andy Cohen Live in 2018, "He hadn't spoken to the parents and one brother for, like, eight months before we started dating."

Aaron reiterated to biographer Ian O'Connor, author of 2024's Out of the Darkness: The Mystery of Aaron Rodgers, that his issues with his family were "deep rooted" and Olivia "has nothing to do with all the years" they haven't spoken.

"There was a lot of times, when I became real famous," Aaron said in Enigma, "where I heard from a lot of people, including family members, who where it was like, ‘Your life is too big, we need you to be smaller. Be smaller, don't talk about your life.'"

Feeling woefully misunderstood, he continued, "It always hurt me because I just feel like you don’t see me. This is not something I ever desired or wanted, other than playing on Sundays. It can definitely change the people around your circle, because it can be intoxicating, the fame and notoriety. So, definitely relationships changed after that. Friendships, family."

Aaron said that, pre-estrangement, he wasn't "super-duper close" with everybody in his family anyway.

"I was close with my little brother," he recalled, referring to younger sibling Jordan Rodgers. "But in actuality it goes back to stuff from high school that kind of made me feel distant. Stuff in college, stuff post-college. And I was quiet about it. 'Cause I thought the best way to do it was, just don’t talk about it publicly. And what do they do?"

In 2016, Jordan appeared on The Bachelorette—and, incidentally, he's been married to rose-bearer JoJo Fletcher since 2022.

When he brought JoJo home to meet his folks and eldest brother Luke Rodgers, there were two empty chairs at the dinner table—purportedly for Aaron and then-girlfriend Olivia—and all of a sudden millions of people found out the Packers QB was estranged from the rest of the family.

"We miss our brother," Luke said on The Bachelorette. "We just are trusting that God brings things full circle. And just wish that everything would just get back to us being a family."

"They go on a bulls--t show and leave two empty chairs," he said in Enigma. "They all agreed this was like a good thing to do, to leave two empty chairs at a stupid dating show that my brother just went on to get famous—his words, not mine—that he ended up winning."

Aaron reiterated in the series that he was never even invited to the dinner, which was held during the NFL season.

A dinner "I was never asked to go to," he said, "not that I would have gone."

E! News reached out to Jordan, Ed and Darla for comment on what Aaron had to say in Enigma but has not yet heard back.

Jordan told E! in 2016 after his hometown episode aired that he "made a commitment to go on there and be honest with JoJo and make sure that she knew everything" about where he was coming from.

Aaron has embraced taking ayahuasca—"It's the hardest medicine possible, that I've tried"—as an essential part of his journey, also touting its healing power for "mind, body, spirit."

"I was searching, for sure," he said in Enigma. "My life was through one lens, of organized religion. Where are people in life finding deep peace and centeredness and presence outside of what I knew?"

Speaking of the divide between him and his family, Aaron said he "found a lot of resistance" once he started researching other religions and plant medicine, "doing things that, compared to what I grew up in, would be considered an alternative lifestyle."

As for his family, he continued, "You know, they’re living as best they can. That is, still engulfed in organized religion, which works for them. That's great. So as much as they might not like what they see, love and respect and gratitude for how I was raised, because it wouldn’t have turned me into who I am today."

"People ask me, 'Is there hope for a reconciliation?'" Aaron said. "I say, 'Yeah, of course. Of course.'"

He added, "I don’t want them to fail, to struggle, to have any strife or issues. I don't wish any ill will on them at all. It's more like this: We're just different steps on the timeline of our own journeys."

#688. Man Utd trigger Fernandes' one-year contract extension

Bruno Fernandes joined Manchester United in 2020

Manchester United have triggered their one-year option on captain Bruno Fernandes' contract.

The 32-year-old's deal was due to expire next summer but sources say both parties decided it was in their best interests to activate the option through to 2028.

It means overseas clubs will not be able to approach Fernandes when the transfer window opens on 1 January.

The Portugal international confirmed on Tuesday that discussions over a new contract had been paused. Sources say they will resume once United's league position has improved.

Fernandes has made 343 appearances for United, scoring 115 goals, since his Â£47m move from Sporting in January 2020.

Last season he broke the Premier League assists record and scooped all of the individual player of the year awards after an outstanding campaign as United finished third.

While there is doubt over his long-term future, extending the contract means United would be able to command a fee for Fernandes should he leave in the summer.

United had been open to selling Fernandes in the summer of 2025, with Saudi Pro-League club Al Hilal offering a huge deal.

After discussing the situation with his wife, Fernandes decided to stay, though he later said it "hurt" United were willing to sell him. He reiterated on Tuesday he was still ambitious to win the biggest honours in the game.

Fernandes is a doubt for Saturday's Premier League encounter with Brentford after returning from the Champions League trip to Sporting with a virus.

The playmaker, who scored both goals in the 2-2 draw with his former club, but did not train on Friday and head coach Mauricio Pochettino said he would take a decision on his captain's fitness on Saturday morning.

"We are going to assess during the day and then tomorrow see how he is when he wakes up," said Pochettino. "We are not going to take any risks."

Pochettino is preparing for his first home game as Man Utd boss

Pochettino was criticised by former Liverpool and England midfielder Jamie Redknapp on the Overlap earlier this week.

Reference was made to the former Tottenham, Paris St-Germain and Chelsea coach high-fiving Sky Sports reporter Patrick Davidson after his side's 4-0 defeat at Liverpool on Sunday, as evidence Pochettino had lost his edge.

"When I saw Pochettino at Southampton and I saw him at Tottenham, he looked like he had that Argentinian dog in him," said Redknapp.

"I look at him now and he's high-fiving everyone, he's got the bracelets on, he's got the barnet. I think he's gone too nice."

It seems someone had mentioned the observation to Pochettino as he went off on a tangent at his Friday news conference when asked about a "crazy" first week that included red cards, refereeing errors, disallowed goals and a drone filming training.

"What are we going to do? Start to cry?" he asked. "No. We have to be strong, believe and keep going. I cannot judge the past. Who am I to do that? I was in Cincinnati. I was outside. I need to shut my mouth, say nothing and start from now.

"Sometimes we are so confusing two words that means something similar; nice and good. I am not nice. We have to be good. It is a different thing. We know when we need to push, when we need to be strong, and when we need to build something to improve the atmosphere and relationship and everything.

Pochettino also confirmed Â£70m midfielder Carlos Baleba is expected to be out until the last week in January with the hamstring injury he sustained against Roma on 3 November.

Forward Marcus Rashford had begun to do individual work outside as he tries to recover from a hip problem that has kept him out since 13 October.

#687. Watch ‘Sesame Street’ Get Festive With an Adorable Spoof of Mariah Carey’s ‘All I Want for Christmas Is You’

All the fuzzy gang wants this holiday season is ... well ... U!

The Muppets of Sesame Street don’t want a lot for Christmas — there’s just one thing they need: literally U!

“If we had no U for Christmas, there’d be no U words you see,” the quartet sings jovially, trading off lines as a green letter U with a Santa hat bounces around to the jolly beat. “We could not unwrap the presents underneath the Christmas tree/ Without words that start with U, the holiday would not feel right/ We couldn’t even untie ribbons/ Or untangle Christmas lights/ Want to unbox Christmas but we can’t/ Won’t you help us understand/ Don’t know what we’ll do/ All we need for Christmas is U!”

Pop superstar Carey’s Christmas staple has so far topped the Hot 100 for 22 weeks since it first reached No. on the Dec. 19, 2019-dated chart, 25 years after the song was originally released. The holiday classic broke the Hot 100’s record for most weeks at No. 1 in December 2025, when it took the summit for a 20th week; it currently boasts 22 weeks at the top spot. (Ella Langley took the record from the Queen of Christmas in September, when “Choosin’ Texas” nabbed its 23rd week at No. 1 on the Hot 100.)

Sesame Street returned for its 57th season on Monday (Nov. 23), and is available via Netflix and PBS Kids.

#685. Chart Rewind: In 2021, Taylor Swift’s Rerecorded ‘All Too Well’ Ruled the Hot 100

The song became the longest No. 1, by run time, among other milestones.

“I was going through a bit of sad time,” Taylor Swift told Jimmy Fallon in 2021 about the lyrics in “All Too Well,” which she cowrote with Liz Rose. “I started ad-libbing what I was going through and what I was feeling.”

Originally released on Swift’s 2012 album Red, at just under five-and-a-half minutes in length, the song became the focus of her rerecorded Red (Taylor’s Version), after growing into a beloved entry in her catalog among Swifties.

“All Too Well (Taylor’s Version)” launched at No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 dated Nov. 27, 2021, as Red (Taylor’s Version) opened atop the Billboard 200.

Two versions made the set: one mirroring its original run time and a 10-minute, 13-second take (both of which combined into one listing on Billboard’s charts). They accompanied the 14-minute, 56-second-long All Too Well: The Short Film, directed by Swift and starring Dylan O’Brien, Sadie Sink and Swift.

Given the longer mix of “All Too Well (Taylor’s Version)” (which led its versions in consumption that week), the song became the longest No. 1 in the Hot 100’s history. Don McLean’s “American Pie (Parts I & II),” at 8 minutes and 37 seconds, had held the mark for nearly a half-century.

Plus, with the original “All Too Well” having charted on the Hot 100, at No. 80, for a week in November 2012, Swift notched the first No. 1 cover of a previously charted Hot 100 hit (not counting samples or interpolations) in more than 20 years, since Christina Aguilera, Lil’ Kim, Mya and P!nk’s “Lady Marmalade” in 2001, after the original by Labelle led for a week in March 1975.

Swift additionally became the first artist to send an update of an act’s own prior Hot 100 hit to No. 1 since Elton John, whose “Candle in the Wind 1997″/”Something About the Way You Look Tonight” reigned for 14 weeks in 1997-98. His live version of “Candle” hit No. 6 in 1988, after he had introduced its studio recording in 1973.

In 2022, All Too Well: The Short Film won the Grammy for best music video. Swift also claimed three Moonpersons for it at the MTV Music Video Awards: video of the year, best longform video and best direction.

In a Q&A at New York City’s Beacon Theatre during the Tribeca Festival in June 2022, Swift reinforced that the expanded “All Too Well” was a gift to her fans, sharing to applause, “You guys just wouldn’t let it go!”
